utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we came across that in an article in the International Herald Tribune.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I note that you put here who fled in the face of, not as a result of. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just a choice of words, mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Chose of words are very important, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fled in the face of or as a result of, I say, would seem to be not too divergent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Fleeing in the face of something is something that happens before something occurs, does it not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or as it occurs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it notes that some of these people are being resettled in other parts of the FRY, meaning the former republic of Yugoslavia and it is noted there, Kosovo, Vojvodina and Sandzak, correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All those are all areas in which there were few or much smaller Serbian populations. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it your knowledge that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was trying to resettle some of these people to boost Serbian populations in those areas?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know if that was a particular plan at this point in time. At that particular point in time when this report was drafted, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: By the way, earlier we had mentioned getting fuel from the United Nations, correct, that the ARSK and/or Serb civilians got fuel from the United Nations. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they had approached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: They did get fuel from the UN, too, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Or do you know?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I understood was that the authorities approached the UN and asked for fuel and vehicles and that the UN was unable to fully satisfy their request.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You worked extensively in Kosovo, did you not, after this fact-finding mission?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You did learn later that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was settling Serbs in Kosovo who came from the Krajina area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the bottom of page 1 you say: "The short duration of the mission and the limited range of motion in the Krajina forced the team to focus on Knin, the so-called capital city of the Krajina," and then you continue on: "The IHF would like to," and then you continue on, on the second page: "Emphasise that because of restrictions of access to the rest of the Krajina, the fact-finding mission was unable to visit other areas of Krajina where reports of violations have been made ... " And I'll stop right there. And if we go down to the footnote, you note that: "The Croatian authorities did not forbid the IHF team to move beyond certain areas outside Knin but, at the same time, said they could not guarantee our security or that we would not be turned back." Now, the limited range of movement was, to some extent, self-imposed by your group. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a degree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the Croatian government did not say, you can't go in this area or we're preventing you from going in this area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In and around Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't prevent you from going outside of Knin, did they?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, in and around Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But if -- you could have gone to Donji Lapac if you had wanted to. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you could have gone do Vrlika and Gracac and other areas within Sector South without any restriction of movement by the Croatian government. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. Those were a little further out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no one prevented you from going there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but we did have to take into consideration the fact that the Croatian military said that the areas were not ultimately -- they couldn't guarantee our safety in that area and that we would not maybe encounter Serb forces that might be hiding in the woods or something like that, hiding in the hills. So we had to weigh practically what we could achieve, where we could go based on the security on the ground and whatever information we were able to obtain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you were not prevented from going anywhere in Knin, were you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of your report, section 1.4, fourth line from the bottom of that section, you say here in your report: "A UN representative alleged that the second wave of looters was comprised of civilian police and 'special police' units." What UN representative told you that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of the UN representatives we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't recall who that was?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that person asked us not to include their name in the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what special police units are referred to as?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Referred to as what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, do you know what they are?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Special police units?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Special police is sort of a broad term, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But in this instance you have no idea what that is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have no idea, so we're taking the information that we gave and I'm just putting it down as a journalist, for instance, would in writing an article, we received this information and we include it as we received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. But did you no independent investigation to determine, for example, whether the special police were even in Knin after the first 31 hours of Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again we were focussed on certain elements here and other aspects of it, as I -- we note that this -- in our introduction is not a comprehensive report and that further investigation would have to be undertaken and that was left to the purview of the Croatian Helsinki Committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So at least far as you're concerned there was no further investigation of what these special police units, for example, were?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the time-frame of this ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 1. -- on section 1.5, again, there are four special police members mentioned. How did you know that they were special police?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they identified themselves as Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing a camouflage-type uniform. They also were wearing, as far as I recall, a -- they had a Ministry of Interior-type patch. I didn't take photographs of them, for instance. They came out of the woods or up the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms on with a Ministry of Interior patch?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of head gear did they have?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall head gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And they -- they identified themselves to you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they identified themselves and asked us what we were doing, and we told them what we were doing and talked to them briefly, and they said, you know, you need to be careful in this area and they suggested that we leave, and we did shortly thereafter, after looking around a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you saw them -- these four people who you term special police members, they were not engaged in anything nefarious or improper that you could see?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I could see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to go further into your report. Actually, I'm done with your report. I'd like to back to your statement, your second statement, P987, on page 6. I'm going to show you, Mr. Hayden, and appreciate you're going to have to be patient with me because it involves dealing with three separate documents. The first is your statement here, P987 which was March of 2004, paragraph 25. Just for your reference to tell you where I'm going, the second document is going to be back to your report at 988 and the third document will be an UNMO report which is P119.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So for the registrar's reference those are the three documents I'm going to refer to. And for the Chamber's reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 25 you note: "In the Kistanje area civilian dressed 'officials' with maps was observed pointing at houses, later some buildings were seen to be burning." And you note here WCH, those are your initials. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "These were the persons who were dressed in civilian dress and were interacting with the uniformed officers." Now I'd like to take you back to P988, which is your report, at section 1.1.1. And in your report, you note: "There is direct evidence of systematic burning and looting of civilian homes and community property, including businesses by the HV, civil police and 'special police units' after the first 31 hours of Operation Storm." Now, later in this paragraph, you note, you say: "On two separate occasions on or around 17/18 August, UN observers saw 'arson teams.'" Now, the second arson team you refer to here is in the Kistanje area civilian dressed 'officials' with maps. That is what you refer to in your second statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you were told this by the UN people that talked to?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go to P119. If we could go to the fourth page of P119. And if we could scroll down to where it says: "The PTL observed ..." Here it says this is an UNMO report from the UN Military Observers. It says the patrol observed at whatever time it is stated there.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "In Kistanje, civilian official looking people with maps, looking and pointing at houses," and your report says these are civilian officials. There's a big difference there, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian official.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Looking.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking people. Just a difference of -- of how it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a big difference, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Du-Toit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DU-TOIT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it should be also pointed out that the report is dated 14th of August, 1995. That is now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's another example of how wrong the report is but he can go into that, I'm going to go into that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There's nothing here that mentions anything about any people in uniform, correct, in this P119 which is in front of you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't, but I wasn't -- wasn't privy to this report, never saw it, and that may not have been the -- the UN official that I spoke with who prepared the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will submit to that you that is the only report that refers to "civilian official looking people or civilian official" in the entire UN and UNMO dossier. So would you agree at least that as of the P119 report, it is different from what it's stated in your report, correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the choice of terms is different. Civilian official looking people or civilian dressed officials and number two is referring to UN observers who saw. So when we spoke with these UN observers, this is what they were telling us, so I didn't have the opportunity to corroborate it by access to this particular sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Nonetheless, those are two difference versions, correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Or I'd like to have called up, please, 3D01-0383. And, Your Honour, just for your reference my last series of questions will relate to this document and another document, and I will leave time for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden, this is a letter from the ICTY to you dated April 19th of 1996. It is asking you to provide, in the second paragraph, detailed witness statement from what you have personally observed and witnessed during your fact-finding mission to the Krajina area last August. Now, would you agree with me, Mr. Hayden, that the statement you gave for the most part contains anecdotes of observations of others rather than facts that you personally observed?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the second page of this particular document, there is under a section called definition on war crime, I'm assuming it should be definition of, there's a laundry list of crimes which is given to you in this letter. Would you agree with me that other than perhaps extensive destruction and appropriation -- extensive destruction, that you did not personally observe any of the other items listed in this particular list?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not personally observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You were asked several questions and you replied that you had given answers to those questions in your first statement. One of the questions is to you why did the civilians leave, did they receive official instructions to do so or did they leave for personal safety reasons. Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some people that we spoke with, particularly those individuals who were in the UN compound, did note that there had been information relayed about evacuation or leaving and others didn't make reference to that and stated that they left for their personal safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it was a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a combination of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, could I seek clarification of the last answer. You said a combination of both. Now I can imagine two situations. One is that citizen A leaves his house because he had heard about plans and is following the suggested plans or the ordered plans and another one is leaving because he feels unsafe. Another scenario is that people hear about evacuation plans or guidance or whatever and feel unsafe and for the two reasons leave their homes. Now if you say it's a combination, what do you mean? That you found both or that you found with the same person knowledge of plans, guidance, et cetera, for evacuation and, at the same time, fear which made them leave their homes? I'm -- the term "combination" is not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that based on the interviews that we had with the displaced persons, again, that there were some who knew or had heard of an evacuation order and were afraid also of what was taking place and presumably made the rational decision to evacuate and others who may have not heard about the order or seen the order but nevertheless knew there was some military operation going on and fled out of fear of their personal safety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And at least a third category, those who just followed what was told without any personal fear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I didn't speak to anyone who mentioned that, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The last document I would like to pull up is 3D01-0386. And before it pops up --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden, I will tell you that this is the second document you received from the ICTY. There it is. It's dated April 29th of 1996. And it's directed to you, Mr. Hayden, and to a Bjorn Engesland?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Engesland.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why it was also directed to Mr. Engesland?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was directed to Mr. Engesland because he was a member of the mission and was also with us in the Krajina, and he is the executive director of the Norwegian Helsinki Committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he give a statement as well?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but based on this I would assume maybe he did give a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you were both asked here, it says dear sirs, I kindly ask you to include in your statement the identity of the following persons and it lists the people who were in the report who were listed as unidentified. You obviously could not identify that person, correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Not by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I note that the date of your statement is May of 1996. Where is the first statement that you sent that the April 29th fax is seeking some clarification to? Because I'm assuming that you received that April 19th which was the previous document the request for a statement, then you gave a statement, and then on April 29th you were asked please identify in your statement the following persons if you can. Where is the first statement.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the only statement that I gave. I don't recall making any other statements other than this statement here from 1996 and then the 2004 statement, so I'm unclear as to the dating of that. I don't have any other statements in my records and I have kept everything since I was first contacted by the Tribunal in a file which included the faxes from Mr. Elfgren.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with that I would just like to move these two documents into evidence. The April 19th letter, 3D01-0383.

utterances.speaker: MR. DU-TOIT
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Du-Toit. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D870.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two together under one exhibit number. D870 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the other document is 3D01-0386.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I moved too quickly. I thought it was included already, which it was not. Mr. Du-Toit, also no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DU-TOIT
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D871 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: One final question, Mr. Hayden, your fact-finding report, is it -- it's a fair assessment, is it not, that the vast majority of material in your report was based on what you heard from others?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM CURTIS HAYDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no other questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Gotovina, no questions. Mr. Du-Toit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DU-TOIT
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you. When you visited the Krajina with your team, did you always stay together or did you move separately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a couple of occasions when we were in Knin where we separated in order to try to set up meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer. Since I have no further questions for you, this concludes your evidence, Mr. Hayden. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first procedural issue I intended to raise was how to proceed with this witness, but that is not -- there is no need anymore for that. Then tomorrow there will be a witness who will testify through videolink. Could I receive estimates on timing because the Chamber needs some time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution expects approximately 45 minutes to an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 45 minutes. Could I hear from Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we expect about an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An hour. Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no questions scheduled at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Me neither, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That leaves us time because there is a small pile of oral decisions and my chamber staff is making us a bit nervous because they're ready, but we didn't find time until now to deliver them, so we'll do that, tomorrow there will be sufficient time. There is another matter, the Prosecution has informed the Chamber and the parties that there are unable to schedule witnesses for 27th and 28th of October. Now, Mr. Mikulicic, from the e-mail I took it that you wanted even a month in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will appreciate that, but unfortunately, that was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there was a mistake. You wanted to know whether we would sit on the 27th and the 28th of October and you are prepared to resume, I do understand, on the 29th of October. Not of November. This is to confirm that we will not sit on the 27th and the 28th of October. I immediately add to that that, of course, that it is of -- not only of some concern, of concern to the Chamber, that we just lose two days in court. I take it there must be very compelling reasons that we will not sit but of course the Chamber is not in a position to -- to find the witnesses the Prosecution could not find. It is it, however, a matter which we might further discuss with the parties briefly, the further scheduling of the case, in the weeks and I rather speak about weeks than about months to come, but we'll leave that for another moment. Are there any other procedural matters? There's -- yes, there is one thing but I think the parties were informed already that on the 27th of November - Mr. Mikulicic, as we are in November now - that we would swap from morning to afternoon. I take it that the parties are informed about that, I take it. Any other matter that could not wait until tomorrow? Then we will adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, the 16th of October, 9.00 in this same courtroom, number I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
